answer: Submissions that land within 209 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The reef detector writes to ocean, and violet shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, and hence the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 298 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 37 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
